name: Many-Tier Instruction Hierarchy (ManyIH)
executive_summary: Extends the flat 4-tier privilege model to arbitrarily many levels for realistic multi-source agentic settings — but benchmarks show even frontier models resolve conflicts correctly only ~40% of the time as tiers scale.
description: Argues the dominant Instruction Hierarchy paradigm (already in this catalog) assumes a fixed, small set of privilege levels (typically fewer than five, defined by rigid role labels like system > user) that's inadequate once real agentic systems have many more instruction sources — system messages, user prompts, tool outputs, other agents — each with genuinely different trust levels that don't collapse cleanly into 4 tiers. Proposes Many-Tier Instruction Hierarchy (ManyIH) as the paradigm for resolving conflicts among arbitrarily many privilege levels, and introduces ManyIH-Bench, the first benchmark for it: 853 agentic tasks (427 coding, 426 instruction-following) requiring navigation of up to 12 levels of conflicting instructions across 46 real-world agent settings. The honest headline finding is a gap, not a solution: even current frontier models perform poorly (~40% accuracy) as instruction conflict scales beyond the traditional 4-tier case.
when_to_use: Multi-agent or multi-tool systems where the 4-tier system/developer/user/tool model is too coarse to represent real differences in trust between many tools, sub-agents, or delegation chains, and you want to benchmark how well a given model actually handles that finer-grained conflict resolution.
when_not_to_use: Simple systems with only the standard system/developer/user/tool distinction — the added tiers are unnecessary complexity, and current models aren't yet demonstrated to handle many-tier conflicts reliably regardless.
known_pitfalls: This is a benchmark and problem framing more than a proven solution — the paper's own headline result is that frontier models handle many-tier conflicts poorly (~40% accuracy), so declaring more privilege tiers in a prompt does not by itself guarantee correct resolution.

primary_source.authors: Zhang, Li, Jurayj, Zhan, Van Durme, Khashabi
primary_source.title: Many-Tier Instruction Hierarchy in LLM Agents
